title: What Is QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping and Is It Worth It?
summary: QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping is Intuit's assisted and full-service bookkeeping offering for QBO users. Here's what's included, the three service tiers, pricing, real limitations, and when it makes sense.
body_markdown:
**QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping is Intuit's add-on service that pairs your QuickBooks Online account with a certified bookkeeper who categorises transactions, reconciles accounts, and closes the books each month.** It's built directly into QBO, so there's no separate software to connect. You pay a monthly fee on top of your QBO subscription for a bookkeeper to handle the work.


This guide covers how QuickBooks Live works, the three service tiers and what each includes, pricing, the real limitations most reviews skip, and how to decide whether it's the right fit for your business.


## What QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping is


QuickBooks Live is a service sold by Intuit that adds bookkeeping support to a QuickBooks Online subscription. Instead of doing the books yourself or hiring a separate bookkeeper, you get access to a QuickBooks-certified bookkeeper who works inside your QBO account.


According to[Intuit's own product page](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/live/) , bookkeepers are matched to your industry and available Monday through Friday. They categorize transactions, reconcile accounts, and meet with you to go over reports.


The service is QBO-only. You must already have an active QuickBooks Online subscription and have filed taxes in the last calendar year to qualify.


## The three QuickBooks Live service tiers


Intuit has reorganised QuickBooks Live into three distinct offerings, and the difference between them matters before you commit.


**Live Expert Assisted** is the entry tier. You keep doing your own books, but a certified bookkeeper is available to answer questions, review your work, and guide you on how to use QuickBooks. It's more coaching than bookkeeping.


**Expert Cleanup** is a one-time service. A bookkeeper reviews your books, fixes errors, and brings everything current for tax time. You pay a one-time fee rather than a recurring subscription. It's designed for businesses that have let their books fall behind.


**Live Expert Full-Service Bookkeeping** is the full-service tier. A dedicated bookkeeper handles your categorisation, reconciliation, and month-end close every month. This is the tier closest to a traditional bookkeeping service.


Most people searching "QuickBooks Live" are thinking about Full-Service, but they're often shown the Assisted tier first. Make sure you're comparing the right option.


## What QuickBooks Live Full Service includes


At the full-service level, your bookkeeper takes over the core monthly tasks. Every month they categorise your transactions, reconcile your bank and card accounts, and close the books. They produce a profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, and they meet with you to review them.


The first month is a cleanup phase. The bookkeeper reviews your existing books, fixes any issues, and brings them current before starting the recurring service.


What's notable is how it's delivered. Everything happens inside your QBO account. The bookkeeper works in the same software you see, so you can check numbers anytime rather than waiting for an emailed report.


## What QuickBooks Live does not include


This is the section most reviews rush past, and it matters. QuickBooks Live Full-Service does not include tax preparation or filing. You still need a separate CPA or tax service for your returns.


Payroll is not included. Neither are accounts payable management, inventory, or any tasks outside of basic bookkeeping. If your books need catch-up beyond the first-month cleanup, that's billed separately.


Bookkeeper availability is capped. They work Monday through Friday within set hours and are split across multiple clients, so you're not getting a dedicated resource who picks up the phone anytime.


It's also only available on QuickBooks Online. QBO Desktop, Solopreneur, or any other version doesn't qualify.


## QuickBooks Live pricing


Intuit prices QuickBooks Live based on your average monthly expenses. The full-service tier starts at around $300 per month for low-expense businesses and rises from there. The Assisted tier is cheaper and often offered as a bundle with certain QBO plans.


The catch is that pricing sits on top of your existing QBO subscription. If you're already paying $85 a month for QBO Essentials and add Full-Service at $300, you're at $385 before any extra cleanup work.


Intuit adjusts pricing regularly, so check current rates before you sign up. Promotional rates for new accounts often apply, but they step up after the intro period.


## QuickBooks Live vs hiring your own bookkeeper


The appeal of QuickBooks Live is convenience. It's inside QBO, it's easy to add, and you don't have to find and vet a bookkeeper yourself.


The trade-off is depth and flexibility. An independent bookkeeper or firm can handle payroll, AP, advisory, and tax prep as a single relationship. QuickBooks Live handles the base tasks only and hands you off to others for everything else.


Cost is worth comparing too. At $300 to $500 a month, QuickBooks Live lands in the same range as many independent bookkeepers who can do more. Our guide to[bookkeeping services fees](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/bookkeeping-services-fees) shows typical ranges so you can run the comparison.


For CPA firms managing clients on QBO, QuickBooks Live is a direct competitor for the monthly bookkeeping work.


The firms that compete well do so by delivering the same clean books faster, with more responsiveness and deeper knowledge of each client's business, which is where[managing 50 clients efficiently](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/manage-50-accounting-clients) becomes a real advantage.


## When QuickBooks Live makes sense


QuickBooks Live is a solid fit for a specific type of business owner: someone on QBO who wants basic monthly bookkeeping handled without shopping for a separate service, doesn't need payroll or tax prep bundled in, and is comfortable with the limited availability and standardised scope.


It makes less sense if you want a bookkeeper who knows your business deeply, need services beyond categorisation and reconciliation, or want more responsiveness than the capped weekly hours provide.


If you're a firm running multiple clients on QBO, you're better served by automation that runs across all of them.


[Finlens](https://www.finlens.app/accountants) automates categorisation, reconciliation, and[month-end close](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/quickbooks-month-end-close-automation) across your whole client book, which is a different model from Intuit's one-client-at-a-time service and one that scales.


## QuickBooks Live vs automation


There's a third option that sits between doing it yourself and paying for a bookkeeper. QBO-native automation handles categorisation, reconciliation, and close automatically, with human review on top.


For businesses that want accurate, current books without the full-service price, automation covers what QuickBooks Live offers at the base level and goes further at the close.


For firms that want to run clean books across many clients at once, it scales in a way a per-client service can't. Our guide to[automating QuickBooks bookkeeping](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/automate-quickbooks-bookkeeping) explains what that looks like in practice.


## Conclusion


QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping is a legitimate option for small business owners who want their monthly books handled without sourcing a separate bookkeeper. The full-service tier covers the basics cleanly, it lives inside QBO, and the setup is simple.


For an owner who just wants the categorisation and reconciliation done each month and doesn't need tax prep or payroll, it does the job.


The limitations are real, though, and worth naming clearly before you buy. Tax filing, payroll, and deep AP management sit outside the service. Bookkeeper availability is capped and shared. Pricing stacks on top of your QBO subscription, and once you add it up against what an independent bookkeeper can do for a similar fee, the value case gets thinner.


The honest decision comes down to what you need. If basic monthly bookkeeping inside QBO is enough, QuickBooks Live is a reasonable choice.


If you want more scope, more responsiveness, or a single relationship that handles the full finance function, an independent bookkeeper or a QBO-specialist firm will serve you better.


And if you're trying to get the same clean books faster and cheaper, modern automation paired with a quick human review is worth comparing before you commit to a recurring service fee.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping?


QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping is an add-on service from Intuit that gives QuickBooks Online users access to a certified bookkeeper. Depending on the tier, the bookkeeper answers questions and guides your work, cleans up past books, or handles monthly categorization, reconciliation, and close on your behalf.


### How much does QuickBooks Live cost?


Full-service pricing starts around $300 a month for low-expense businesses and increases with your monthly expense volume. This is in addition to your QuickBooks Online subscription. Intuit adjusts pricing often, so verify current rates before signing up. Promotional intro rates are common but step up after the first period.


### What does QuickBooks Live Full-Service include?


It includes monthly transaction categorization, bank and card reconciliation, month-end close, and financial statement delivery. The first month includes a cleanup of your existing books. It does not include tax preparation, payroll, accounts payable management, or catch-up bookkeeping beyond the initial cleanup.


### Does QuickBooks Live do your taxes?


No. QuickBooks Live Bookkeeping does not prepare or file tax returns. You still need a separate CPA or tax service for that. The service keeps your books clean and current, which makes tax prep easier, but the filing itself is outside the scope.


### Is QuickBooks Live worth it?


It depends on your situation. If you want basic monthly bookkeeping inside QBO without sourcing a separate provider, it's a convenient option. If you need payroll, tax prep, or deeper advisory, an independent bookkeeper or firm can do more for a similar price. Compare the full cost, scope, and availability before deciding.


### What is the difference between QuickBooks Live Assisted and Full-Service?


Assisted is coaching. You do your own books and a bookkeeper answers questions and guides you. Full-Service is hands-off. The bookkeeper handles your categorization, reconciliation, and close each month. Expert Cleanup is a separate one-time service to fix and update books for tax time.


### Can a CPA firm use QuickBooks Live for clients?


QuickBooks Live is designed for individual business owners, not for firms managing multiple client accounts. Firms looking to deliver the same clean monthly books across a client base are better served by automation tools built for multi-client QBO workflows.


### What are the alternatives to QuickBooks Live?


The main alternatives are an independent bookkeeper or accounting firm, full-service online bookkeeping providers, and QBO-native automation tools. Each trades off differently on price, scope, and responsiveness. The right choice depends on how much service you need and how hands-off you want to be.
